pill.desc: white lyophilized powder in a single-dose vial

tell: A peptibody that activates the TPO receptor; its serum levels fall when platelet counts are high.

clues.text: Its elimination is partly dependent on its receptor on platelets, so patients with high platelet counts have low serum concentrations.
Supplied as a sterile lyophilized powder, reconstituted with sterile water to a concentration of 500 mcg/mL.
Approved under a BLA in 125, 250 and 500 mcg single-dose vials, given once weekly.
No boxed warning and no contraindications. Headache is the most commonly reported adverse reaction versus placebo; in children, contusion is among the most common.
Immune thrombocytopenia that has not responded to corticosteroids, immunoglobulins or splenectomy, and survival after acute exposure to myelosuppressive radiation.
Binds and activates the TPO receptor, increasing platelet production by a mechanism analogous to endogenous TPO.
The generic name begins with R and has eleven letters.
